title: Pilot round 2: 14 redrawn cards
ask: Drawn under the new rules: speakers look at each other, the scene stays consistent across panels, and hands belong to the right people. Each card sits next to its round-1 picture and your note. The automatic check passed 3 and flagged 8 as borderline. Three still fail after two retries because of how they were staged: A2-0114 kiek and A2-0895 geros kelionės (neighbour test), and A2-0881 atsiprašau (the staged bowed head can never meet the other person's eyes). The page also shows phrase backs with the new usage notes.

title: 10 usage notes Fable couldn't source
ask: 70 sourced notes are already on the phrase backs. These 10 weren't backed by a source Fable could read: the synonym clusters žinoma / aišku / be abejo, akimirką / minutėlė, puiku / šaunu / nuostabus, plus nieko baisaus and Kiek tai kainuoja? Your Lithuanian is the best check here.
detail:
| Card | Lithuanian | Draft note |
|---|---|---|
| A2-1185 | nieko baisaus | It's nothing / never mind (lit. 'nothing terrible'): fills the same slot as nieko tokio, reassuring someone who apologises or worries. |
| A2-0883 | Žinoma | Of course — the neutral agreement word (lit. 'known'). Aišku is brisker ('clear!'), be abejo ('without doubt') more emphatic. |
| A2-1148 | aišku | Of course; clearly — as an answer, a brisk colloquial 'sure, obviously'; as an adverb, 'clearly'. Neutral cousin: žinoma. |
| A2-1172 | be abejo | Undoubtedly / of course — 'without doubt'; a shade more emphatic and formal than žinoma. |
| A2-0884 | Akimirką | Just a moment — accusative of akimirka 'an instant'; a shop assistant's or receptionist's word. Minutėlę! is the warmer diminutive twin; both fit tu and jūs. |
| A2-1169 | minutėlė | Just a minute — said as Minutėlę! (accusative), the diminutive making it friendly; akimirką is the plainer twin. |
| A2-1154 | puiku | Great! — neuter adjective used as an exclamation; neutral register. Šaunu is more colloquial, nuostabu/nuostabus stronger ('wonderful'), labai gerai the sober 'very good'. |
| A2-1156 | šaunu | Cool! / great! — colloquial, youthful; puiku is the neutral equivalent. Šaunuolis (the person) is 'good lad / well done'. |
| A2-1465 | nuostabus | Wonderful — stronger than puiku; as an exclamation the neuter nuostabu! The card's form is the masculine adjective. |
| A2-0899 | Kiek tai kainuoja? | How much is it? — the same question as Kiek kainuoja? with tai ('this/that') said out loud; one picture serves both. |
